thinking_and_logic: The solution maintains a hash map from previously seen number to its index. For each element n at index i, it computes complement = target - n and checks whether that complement has already appeared; if so, the pair of indices is immediately returned. Checking before inserting the current element ensures you never use the same element twice.
code_assessment: Your final code is essentially identical to the canonical optimal approach in the answer key (single-pass hash map, complement check before insert). It directly avoids the known pitfalls listed (same element twice and sorting away original indices) and meets the expected O(n) time / O(n) space profile.
